quote: Bestimmung der Zahl der Primzahlproducte $pq$ welche $< n$ sind.
english: Determination of the number of prime products pq which are < n.
topic: The page poses counting the prime products pq below n, gives a remark on the nature of number as the bearer of a rule or a 'wandering cut', and states an axiom for passing from number to geometric magnitude by mapping all numbers one-to-one onto a curve.

triage.modern_statement: Find the counting function of semiprimes, π₂(x) = #{n ≤ x : n = pq with p, q prime}, or at least its asymptotic behaviour. Depending on the convention, p = q may be allowed, or the two primes may be required to be distinct. In modern terms this is the case k = 2 of counting k-almost primes (integers with exactly k prime factors) up to x. The expected answer is π₂(x) ~ x·log log x / log x.
triage.answered_by: Edmund Landau in 1900. He proved that the number of k-almost primes up to x is asymptotic to x(log log x)^{k-1}/((k-1)! log x), which for k = 2 gives x log log x / log x. He later found asymptotic expansions with error O(x/log^m x). Later work includes more elementary proofs (S. M. Shah, S. Selberg), generalisations by Delange and Tenenbaum, and a full asymptotic expansion of π₂(x) by Crişan and Erban.

evidence.claim: Asymptotics for the number of integers ≤ x with exactly k prime factors are called a classic question in analytic number theory that was originally resolved by Landau in 1900.
By a 1900 theorem of Landau, the number of k-almost primes not exceeding x is asymptotic to x(log log x)^{k-1}/((k-1)! log x). Recent papers prove numerically explicit bounds around this formula.
Landau later found asymptotic expansions for π_k(x) and σ_k(x) with error O(x log^{-m} x) for any m. S. M. Shah and S. Selberg later obtained similar results by more elementary methods.
Crişan and Erban derived an asymptotic series for the semiprime counting function π₂(x) using a combinatorial argument. It generalises earlier results of Landau, Delange and Tenenbaum.
An Oxford talk covers an asymptotic expansion for the semiprime counting function, generalising earlier findings of Landau, Delange and Tenenbaum.

triage.why: The note states the problem clearly: count the semiprimes pq below n. This is the k = 2 case of a classical problem that Landau solved asymptotically in 1900. I found no source tying it to Hilbert's 23 problems or the 24th problem. The note does not say whether Hilbert wanted an exact formula or an asymptotic, but the standard modern reading is the asymptotic, and that is settled. Work continues on finer expansions and explicit bounds (e.g. the Crişan–Erban expansion and explicit bounds for 3-almost primes), so the area is still mildly active, though the basic question is closed. I don't know the page's date, so I can't say whether Hilbert wrote this before or after Landau's result.
